brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
Songyang Cha is the green tea of Songyang County in Zhejiang, known for four qualities: green colour, tight strands, high aroma and strong flavour. Its best-known representative is Songyang Yinhou.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: A Ming-dynasty verse is cited as praising the tea of Songyang, and in 1929 it took a first prize at the West Lake Exposition. The Yinhou line, associated with the Xiehou Mountain area on the upper Ou River, includes Yinhou Shanlan, Yinhou Longjian, Yinhou Baicha and Yinhou Xiangcha.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight strands with a lustrous emerald colour.
taste_profile: Lasting high aroma and a full, brisk flavour.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
